partners.diseaseBName: combined immunodeficiency due to OX40 deficiency
partners.mechanism_chain: EDARADD (HGNC:17305) —LEADS_TO→ Hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia with or without intellectual disability (HP:0001055); TNFRSF4 (HGNC:11509) —DISRUPTS→ T cell activation and proliferation (GO:0042110); T cell activation and proliferation (GO:0042110) —LEADS_TO→ Combined immunodeficiency (HP:0002695). #### 1. ectodermal dysplasia 11B, hypohidrotic/hair/tooth type, autosomal recessive  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.734)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:14341)

**Proposed mechanism:** EDARADD (HGNC:14341) —DISRUPTS→ Ectodermal development and hair follicle morphogenesis (GO:0007408); Ectodermal development and hair follicle morphogenesis (GO:0007408) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal hair physiology (HP:0002371); Ectodermal development and hair follicle morphogenesis (GO:0007408) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal tooth morphology (HP:0000160); Ectodermal development and hair follicle morphogenesis (GO:0007408) —LEADS_TO→ Hypohidrosis (HP:0000989). Loss-of-function mutations in EDARADD disrupt the ectodermal development and hair follicle morphogenesis pathway, leading to the shared phenotypes of abnormal hair, abnormal tooth morphology, and hypohidrosis observed in both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of pathogenic variants in EDARADD with a gain-of-function mechanism in either disease, or if the shared phenotypes can be attributed to distinct, non-overlapping pathways not affected by EDARADD. _(variant: Any common variant (AF > 0.01) in EDARADD present in gnomAD.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of EDARADD in these ectodermal dysplasias could lead to targeted therapeutic strategies for improving hair, tooth, and sweat gland function in affected individuals.
